description: A security engineering manager must finalize the rollout plan for a critical authentication-library patch across internet-facing services, including the canary window, service handling, staffing, and compliance evidence.

shared_context.S1: The authentication-library patch addresses a critical vulnerability and has passed the security team's laboratory tests.
shared_context.S2: The current draft rollout proposes a Thursday 02:00 UTC canary lasting 60 minutes, followed by broad deployment on Friday.
shared_context.S3: Riley makes the binding decision on the production rollout plan.
shared_context.S4: The team's release policy requires a final round-robin check with application platform, reliability, and compliance before a security rollout plan is approved.

PF1.text: While debugging an unrelated authentication test this morning, Mei confirmed that the Ledger service uses a custom fork of the library; Ledger must have the compatibility flag enabled before broad deployment, and it must be excluded from the canary until that flag is enabled. She has not updated the rollout document because the compatibility test completed only minutes ago.

PF2.text: Jonah checked the current on-call rota while preparing another maintenance window and confirmed that he is the only engineer qualified to perform rollback for this patch during Wednesday 18:00-22:00 UTC; the Thursday 02:00 UTC slot has no qualified rollback engineer. He has not posted the staffing confirmation because the rota change is still being recorded.

PF3.text: Daria confirmed with the audit team this afternoon that evidence showing every internet-facing service patched is due by Friday 12:00 UTC, and an exception would not satisfy this review. She has not added the requirement to the security ticket because the audit team's written confirmation arrived minutes ago.

acceptance_conditions: The canary must move to Wednesday.
The canary must start at exactly 18:00 UTC.
The canary must last exactly 120 minutes.
Ledger must be excluded from the canary.
Ledger's compatibility flag must be enabled before broad rollout.
Every internet-facing service must be patched by Friday 12:00 UTC.
A compatibility-work commitment for Ledger must be recorded.
A qualified rollback-staffing commitment naming Jonah must be recorded.
A compliance-evidence commitment for all internet-facing services must be recorded.
The Ledger compatibility finding must be cited as justification.

content_checks.C8: any(c['type'] == 'qualified_rollback_staffing' and c['target'] == 'Jonah' for c in commitments)
content_checks.C9: any(c['type'] == 'compliance_evidence' and c['target'] == 'all internet-facing services' for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The custom Ledger fork changes the service treatment from ordinary canary participation to canary exclusion, requires the compatibility flag before broad rollout, and creates the Ledger compatibility-work commitment.
Jonah's qualification window changes the canary from Thursday 02:00 UTC to Wednesday 18:00 UTC and requires a rollback-staffing commitment naming Jonah.
The audit confirmation changes the completion requirement to every internet-facing service by exactly Friday 12:00 UTC and creates the compliance-evidence commitment.
